Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $p=⟨-1,1,2⟩$ and $q=⟨4,x,1⟩.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =(-1)\cdot 4+1\cdot x+2\cdot 1 \\  & =x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ x-2 & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
